judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amended identification is built on open-ended catch-alls — 'related topics such as oil drilling, technology and infrastructure' and the negative carve-out 'not including information concerning asset management and investment advice relating to stocks and bonds' — whose reach is genuinely contestable, and the first (electronic publications) item omits any class designation while the parallel items end 'in Class 16' and 'in Class 36'; the word 'worldwide' also appears in the electronic item but not the printed one. Those are nameable general-vs-specific and mechanical defects on the face of the paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Background recital says the application was published in International Classes 9, 16 and 36, yet paragraph 1's operative list identifies only Classes 16 and 36, leaving the Class 9 goods unassigned — a recital-versus-operative mismatch; paragraph 2's covenant expressly incorporates 'the goods and services as set forth in that application as amended pursuant to paragraph 1', so any gap in this list propagates into the covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant is specific as to PETROLEUM ARGUS 'as shown in that application for the goods and services as set forth in that application as amended', then closes with the wholly open catch-all 'or do any act or thing in derogation thereof' — a classic general-against-specific tension, and the enumeration invites an expressio unius argument that marks or goods not listed (e.g. ARGUS standing alone) are outside the promise. The scope of 'contest or challenge' versus mere non-opposition is also contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against paragraph 3 (which covers ENERGY ARGUS registrations) and paragraph 1 (which fixes the goods), the two covenants together define a closed universe of protected marks, so whether the instrument as a whole restrains conduct outside that universe is a live whole-instrument question; the merger clause in paragraph 6 forecloses resort to extrinsic understandings to fill the gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same structure as paragraph 2: enumerated registrations and 'the goods and services as set forth in the registrations' followed by the indeterminate 'or do any act or thing in derogation thereof', and the operative mark is described as 'ENERGY ARGUS' while the registrations are for 'ENERGY ARGUS & Design' — a slippage that changes what is covered. Both the catch-all and the mark description are nameable defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against paragraph 2 and paragraph 1: nothing in the agreement addresses Petroleum Argus's use of ARGUS alone or of any other mark, so the pairing of these two covenants is what generates the argument that the instrument was exhaustive of the parties' trademark peace. That is a relationship-level rather than a purely textual issue, but no direct contradiction with another clause appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is ungrammatical — 'the performance of shall be governed' drops its object — and the second sentence, 'This provision extends to the United States, its territories and possessions', is opaque: it is unclear whether it enlarges the choice of law, the parties' substantive obligations, or the territorial reach of the covenants. 'This provision' is a nameable ambiguous referent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: If 'This provision' is read as a territorial statement it interacts with paragraphs 2 and 3, whose covenants are otherwise tied to U.S. trademark filings, but nothing else in the instrument defines geographic scope, so the fit is uncertain rather than contradictory. No clause directly conflicts with the New York choice of law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line successors clause, but 'licensees' is an unusual addition whose effect — whether a licensee of Petroleum Argus takes the benefit of the paragraph 2 and 3 covenants, and whether it is correspondingly bound — is genuinely contestable. The clause never says which affiliates or related entities count.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against paragraphs 2 and 3, which run only between the two named corporations: if a licensee or successor entity uses the marks, whether the covenants reach it turns wholly on this clause, so the interaction is real though not a contradiction. Nothing in the agreement defines 'successors' or excludes affiliates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional merger-plus-written-modification clause; 'This is the entire agreement' is terse but its meaning is standard and neither term is genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the Background recital, which frames the deal as resolving a 'potential dispute'; the merger clause bars extrinsic gloss on the covenants in paragraphs 2 and 3 but does not contradict any operative term. Its main effect is to sharpen other clauses' ambiguity rather than create its own.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'costs in attorneys' fees' is almost certainly a mistyping of 'costs and attorneys' fees', and the error changes meaning — as written it covers only costs incurred in attorneys' fees rather than costs plus fees. That is a nameable mechanical defect, though the stakes in fighting over it are small.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No fee-shifting, indemnity or enforcement provision appears anywhere else in the agreement, so there is nothing for this clause to contradict; whether it covers fees in a future enforcement action is unaddressed but not inconsistent with any other term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The parties will agree to keep' reads as an agreement to agree rather than a present obligation, and the exception 'as required by Court order and/or state and federal rules of civil procedure' is a broad, ill-bounded carve-out sitting against a narrow specific ('Court order'). Both the futurity of the promise and the reach of the exception are nameable problems.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against paragraph 1, which requires a public amendment of a USPTO application, and against paragraphs 2 and 3, whose enforcement would require disclosing the agreement's terms — confidentiality is in tension with the agreement's own public-record mechanics, though not squarely contradicted by any clause.
